intro: Attention turns similarities into a weighted mixture of values. A mask defines which keys a query is allowed to use, such as only earlier tokens.
task: Return a dictionary with weights and output for scaled dot-product attention. A True mask entry permits attention.
requirements: Q has shape (m,d), K (n,d), V (n,v), and boolean mask (m,n), with positive dimensions.
Scale scores by sqrt(d), apply the mask, and use a numerically stable softmax per row.
An entirely masked row must have zero weights and zero output.
Reject incompatible shapes, non-boolean masks, or non-finite inputs with ValueError. Do not mutate inputs; test dot products are representable.

hints.title: Separate allowed positions
hints.body: Replace disallowed scores with -infinity, then identify rows with at least one permitted key.

hints.title: Stabilize each row
hints.body: Subtract a row maximum before exponentiation. Give entirely masked rows a safe maximum such as zero.

hints.title: Divide only where valid
hints.body: Use a zero-filled result and divide where the denominator is positive. Multiply the weights by V.

explanation: The dot products measure query-key compatibility. Scaling by the square root of the key dimension moderates their growth as the dimension increases.
Masking happens before normalization. Zeroing probabilities afterward would leave valid rows with weights that no longer sum to one.
An entirely masked row has no probability distribution. This exercise defines a zero result so downstream code gets an explicit, finite outcome.
